name: Pharaoh enslaves the Israelites with harsh labor
summary: A new king who does not remember Joseph fears Israel's growing numbers and forces them into hard labor.

name: Pharaoh orders Hebrew midwives to kill baby boys
summary: Pharaoh secretly instructs the Hebrew midwives Shiphrah and Puah to kill every son born to Israelite mothers.

name: Shiphrah and Puah defy Pharaoh's order
summary: The midwives fear God and let the baby boys live, then tell Pharaoh the Hebrew women give birth too quickly for them to intervene.

name: Pharaoh commands Hebrew infant boys drowned in the Nile
summary: After the midwives refuse to obey, Pharaoh orders all his people to throw every newborn Hebrew boy into the Nile.

name: Moses is born and hidden by his mother
summary: A Levite couple has a son and Jochebed hides him for three months to protect him from Pharaoh's decree.

name: Moses is placed in a basket on the Nile
summary: Unable to hide him any longer, Jochebed sets Moses adrift in a papyrus basket among the reeds while Miriam watches, until Pharaoh's daughter comes down to the river and finds him.

name: Pharaoh's daughter adopts Moses as her son
summary: Pharaoh's daughter has Jochebed nurse the baby, then takes him as her own son and raises him in the Egyptian royal household.

name: Moses kills an Egyptian and flees to Midian
summary: As an adult, Moses kills an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew and, when it becomes known, flees to Midian to escape Pharaoh.

name: Moses marries Zipporah at a well in Midian
summary: Moses helps the daughters of the priest of Midian at a well, and their father Jethro gives Moses his daughter Zipporah in marriage.

name: The king of Egypt dies and God remembers his covenant
summary: Years pass, the king of Egypt dies, and Israel groans under slavery and cries out; God hears them and remembers his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

name: God appears to Moses in the burning bush
summary: While shepherding Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses sees a bush on fire that is not consumed and turns aside to look.

name: God commissions Moses to deliver Israel
summary: God tells Moses that he has seen Israel's suffering and sends him to Pharaoh to bring the people out of Egypt.

name: God reveals his name to Moses
summary: When Moses asks what name to give Israel, God answers "I AM WHO I AM" and identifies himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

name: God gives Moses miraculous signs to perform
summary: God turns Moses' staff into a snake and makes his hand leprous and clean again as proof for Israel that God sent him.

name: Moses objects that he is slow of speech
summary: Moses protests that he is not a skilled speaker, and God grows angry but agrees to give him Aaron as a spokesman.

name: God appoints Aaron to speak for Moses
summary: God tells Moses that his brother Aaron is already on his way to meet him and will speak to the people on his behalf.

name: Moses and Aaron reunite at the mountain of God
summary: Moses leaves Midian with his family, and Aaron meets him at the mountain of God (Horeb), where Moses tells him all that the LORD has said.

name: Moses and Aaron gather Israel's elders in Egypt
summary: Back in Egypt, Aaron speaks to the elders of Israel and performs the signs, and the people believe and worship.

name: Moses and Aaron demand Pharaoh release Israel
summary: Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh that the LORD demands he let Israel go into the wilderness to worship, and Pharaoh refuses.

name: Pharaoh increases the Israelites' labor burden
summary: Pharaoh punishes the request by forcing the Israelites to gather their own straw while still producing the same quota of bricks.

name: God renews his covenant promise to Moses
summary: After Moses complains that conditions have worsened, God reaffirms his covenant name and his promise to bring Israel out of slavery into the land.

name: Moses and Aaron are commissioned again to confront Pharaoh
summary: Despite Moses' discouragement, God sends him and Aaron back to Pharaoh to demand Israel's release.

name: Aaron's staff swallows the magicians' staffs
summary: Aaron's staff becomes a serpent before Pharaoh and swallows the staffs of Egypt's magicians, yet Pharaoh's heart stays hard.

name: The Nile turns to blood
summary: Aaron strikes the Nile with his staff and the river and all its water turn to blood, killing the fish.

name: Frogs overrun the land of Egypt
summary: Frogs swarm out of the Nile and fill Egyptian houses until Pharaoh begs Moses to remove them and briefly agrees to let Israel go.

name: The dust becomes gnats throughout Egypt
summary: Aaron strikes the dust and it turns to gnats on people and animals across Egypt, a plague even Pharaoh's magicians cannot copy.

name: Swarms of flies invade Egypt but spare Goshen
summary: Dense swarms of flies fill Egyptian homes while the land of Goshen, where Israel lives, is untouched.

name: A plague kills the Egyptians' livestock
summary: A severe plague kills the horses, donkeys, camels, herds, and flocks of Egypt while none of Israel's animals die.

name: Boils break out on the Egyptians
summary: Moses throws soot into the air and painful boils break out on the Egyptians and their animals throughout the land.

name: Hail devastates the crops and livestock of Egypt
summary: A destructive hailstorm mixed with fire strikes Egypt, flattening crops and killing people and animals left in the open.

name: Locusts strip Egypt's remaining crops
summary: A vast swarm of locusts covers the land and eats every plant the hail left standing.

name: Darkness covers the land of Egypt for three days
summary: A thick darkness settles over Egypt for three days while Israel's homes remain filled with light.

name: God warns Moses of the coming death of the firstborn
shortName: God warns of the firstborn's death
summary: Before the final plague, God tells Moses that every firstborn in Egypt will die and Pharaoh will finally drive Israel out.

name: God institutes the Passover meal and instructions
summary: God gives Moses and Aaron detailed instructions for the Passover meal and the blood on the doorframes that will protect Israel's homes.

name: The tenth plague strikes every firstborn in Egypt
summary: At midnight the LORD strikes down every firstborn in Egypt, from Pharaoh's household to the prisoner's, and Pharaoh finally releases Israel.

name: Israel departs Egypt from Rameses
summary: The Israelites, roughly six hundred thousand men plus women and children, leave Rameses for Succoth after four hundred thirty years in Egypt.

name: God commands the consecration of the firstborn
summary: God instructs Moses that every firstborn male among Israel's people and animals belongs to the LORD as a reminder of the exodus.

name: A pillar of cloud and fire leads Israel
shortName: The pillar of cloud and fire
summary: God leads Israel away from the shorter Philistine road and guides the people with a visible pillar of cloud by day and fire by night.

name: Pharaoh pursues Israel with his army
summary: Pharaoh changes his mind and chases Israel with chariots, trapping the people between his army and the sea.

name: Israel crosses the Red Sea on dry ground
summary: Moses stretches out his hand, the LORD drives back the sea with a strong wind, and Israel walks across on dry ground.

name: The sea closes over Pharaoh's army
summary: As the Egyptian army follows into the seabed, the waters return and drown Pharaoh's entire chariot force.

name: Moses and Miriam lead Israel in a song of triumph
summary: Moses and Israel sing praise to the LORD for drowning Pharaoh's army in the sea, and Miriam leads the women in dance with tambourines.

name: The LORD sweetens Israel's bitter water
summary: Three days into the wilderness, Israel finds only bitter water at Marah, and the LORD shows Moses a log that makes the water sweet.

name: Israel camps at an oasis of springs and palm trees
summary: Israel travels on from Marah and camps at Elim, where there are twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees.

name: Israel grumbles that they will starve
summary: Israel complains against Moses and Aaron that they will starve, wishing they had died in Egypt where there was bread to eat.

name: The LORD provides quail and manna from heaven
summary: The LORD sends quail to cover the camp each evening and a flake-like bread called manna on the ground each morning for Israel to gather.

name: The LORD establishes a Sabbath pattern through the manna
summary: Moses instructs Israel to gather double on the sixth day and none on the seventh, and some who go out looking for manna on the Sabbath find none.

name: Israel quarrels with Moses over water at Rephidim
summary: Camped at Rephidim with no water, the people quarrel with Moses and accuse him of bringing them out of Egypt to die of thirst.

name: Moses strikes the rock and water flows out
summary: The LORD tells Moses to strike a rock at Horeb with his staff, and water flows out for the people to drink.

name: Israel defeats Amalek while Moses holds up his hands
summary: Israel prevails in battle against Amalek as long as Moses' hands stay lifted, so Aaron and Hur hold his hands up until sunset.

name: Jethro brings Zipporah and Moses' sons to him
summary: Jethro comes to Moses in the wilderness with Zipporah and their sons and rejoices to hear all the LORD has done for Israel.

name: Jethro sees Moses judging the people alone all day
summary: Jethro watches Moses sit as judge over the people from morning until evening, settling every dispute by himself.

name: Jethro advises Moses to appoint capable men as judges
summary: Jethro tells Moses to appoint capable, God-fearing men over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, bringing only the hardest cases to himself.

name: The LORD proposes a covenant with Israel at Sinai
summary: The LORD tells Moses that if Israel obeys and keeps his covenant, they will be his treasured possession and a kingdom of priests.

name: Israel consecrates itself and boundaries are set around Sinai
summary: Moses consecrates the people, has them wash their garments, and sets a boundary around the mountain that no one may cross on pain of death.

name: The LORD descends on Sinai in thunder, fire, and smoke
summary: On the third day, thunder and lightning strike the mountain, a thick cloud and trumpet blast sound, and the LORD descends on Sinai in fire so that the whole mountain quakes.

name: God speaks the Ten Commandments to Israel
summary: God speaks the Ten Commandments aloud to Israel from the mountain, beginning with his rescue of them from slavery in Egypt.

name: The terrified people ask Moses to speak for God
summary: Overwhelmed by the thunder and lightning, the people beg Moses to speak to them himself rather than have God speak directly, for fear they will die.

name: The LORD gives laws on servants and personal injury
shortName: Eye for eye, tooth for tooth
summary: The LORD gives case laws covering Hebrew servants and compensation for injury, including the principle of eye for eye and tooth for tooth.

name: The LORD gives laws protecting property and the vulnerable
summary: The LORD gives laws on restitution for theft, protection for widows, orphans, and sojourners, and lending to the poor without interest.

name: The LORD commands justice and institutes the three annual feasts
summary: The LORD commands impartial justice for the poor, rest for the land every seventh year, and three feasts Israel must keep before him each year.

name: The LORD promises to send his angel ahead of Israel
summary: The LORD promises to send his angel to guard Israel and bring them into Canaan, warning them not to worship or make a covenant with the gods of that land.

name: Israel ratifies the covenant with sprinkled blood
summary: Israel agrees to all the LORD's words, and Moses builds an altar, sprinkles blood on the people, and calls it the blood of the covenant.

name: Moses, Aaron, and seventy elders see the God of Israel
summary: Moses, Aaron, and seventy elders go up the mountain, see the God of Israel, and eat and drink in his presence.

name: Moses enters the cloud on the mountain for forty days
summary: Moses goes up into the cloud covering the mountain, where the glory of the LORD appears like a consuming fire, and stays forty days and nights.

name: The LORD instructs Moses to build the ark, table, and lampstand
summary: The LORD calls for a freewill offering and gives Moses detailed plans for the ark of the covenant, the table for the bread of the Presence, and the golden lampstand.

name: The LORD gives instructions for the tabernacle's structure
summary: The LORD gives detailed plans for the tabernacle's curtains, wooden frames, and coverings, and for the veil separating the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.

name: The LORD gives instructions for the bronze altar and courtyard
summary: The LORD gives plans for the bronze altar of burnt offering and the courtyard that will surround the tabernacle.

name: The LORD gives instructions for the priestly garments
summary: The LORD gives plans for Aaron's sacred garments, including the ephod and the breastpiece of judgment set with twelve stones for Israel's tribes.

name: The LORD gives instructions for ordaining Aaron and his sons
summary: The LORD gives detailed instructions for the seven-day ceremony that will ordain Aaron and his sons as priests.

name: The LORD gives instructions for the incense altar and basin
summary: The LORD gives plans for the altar of incense, the bronze basin for washing, and the recipes for the anointing oil and incense reserved for sacred use.

name: The LORD appoints craftsmen filled with his Spirit
summary: The LORD fills craftsmen with his Spirit and skill to build the tabernacle and everything in it, and reaffirms the Sabbath as a lasting sign of the covenant.

name: The LORD gives Moses the two tablets of the testimony
summary: When he finishes speaking with Moses on the mountain, the LORD gives him two stone tablets written by the finger of God.

name: Israel persuades Aaron to make a golden calf
summary: When Moses delays on the mountain, the people press Aaron to make gods for them, and he casts their gold earrings into an idol shaped like a calf.

name: Moses intercedes and the LORD relents from destroying Israel
summary: The LORD tells Moses he will destroy Israel and make a great nation from Moses instead, but Moses pleads on the people's behalf and the LORD relents.

name: Moses breaks the tablets and destroys the golden calf
summary: Seeing the calf and the people's revelry, Moses throws down and breaks the tablets, burns the calf, grinds it to powder, and makes the people drink it.

name: The Levites side with Moses and execute judgment on the guilty
summary: Moses calls for whoever is on the LORD's side, the Levites gather to him, and about three thousand of the guilty are put to death that day.

name: The LORD says he will not personally go with Israel
summary: The LORD tells Moses he will send an angel ahead but will not go among the stiff-necked people himself, lest he consume them, and the people mourn.

name: Moses meets with the LORD face to face at the tent of meeting
summary: Moses pitches a tent of meeting outside the camp, and the LORD speaks with him there face to face, as a man speaks with his friend.

name: Moses pleads for the LORD's presence and asks to see his glory
summary: Moses asks the LORD not to send Israel onward without his presence, and then asks to see the LORD's glory.

name: The LORD proclaims his name and character to Moses
summary: The LORD passes before Moses on the mountain and proclaims himself the LORD, merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.

name: The LORD renews the covenant with Israel
summary: Moses asks the LORD to forgive and go with the people, and the LORD renews his covenant, repeating commands about worship, the feasts, and the Sabbath.

name: Moses' face shines and he wears a veil before the people
summary: After forty days on the mountain, Moses comes down with his face shining from speaking with the LORD, and he wears a veil except when he speaks with him.

name: Israel brings freewill offerings to build the tabernacle
summary: Moses calls for a freewill offering, and everyone whose heart is stirred brings gold, silver, bronze, yarns, wood, oil, and gems for the tabernacle.

name: The people give more than enough and Moses restrains them
summary: The people keep bringing gifts morning after morning until the craftsmen tell Moses they have more than enough, and Moses commands them to stop.

name: The ark, table, lampstand, and altar of incense are built
summary: The ark of the covenant with its mercy seat and cherubim, the table, the golden lampstand, and the altar of incense are built exactly as the LORD commanded Moses.

name: The bronze altar and courtyard are built
summary: The bronze altar and the tabernacle's courtyard are built, and the exact amounts of gold, silver, and bronze Israel contributed are recorded.

name: The priestly garments are finished exactly as commanded
summary: Aaron's priestly garments are finished exactly as the LORD commanded Moses, down to the gold plate engraved "Holy to the LORD."

name: Moses inspects the finished work and blesses the people
summary: The finished tabernacle work is brought to Moses, and after inspecting it he sees it is all done as the LORD commanded and blesses the people.

name: Moses sets up the tabernacle exactly as commanded
summary: Moses sets up the tabernacle, arranges its furnishings in their place, and anoints it with the anointing oil to consecrate it, exactly as the LORD commanded.

name: The glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle
summary: A cloud covers the tent of meeting and the glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle so completely that Moses is not able to enter it.

name: The cloud of the LORD guides Israel's ongoing journeys
summary: Whenever the cloud lifts from the tabernacle, Israel sets out on its journeys, and when it does not lift, the people stay in camp.
